output.summary: Audit the README against the implementation tip and correct its opening, capture/owner-decision wording, capability compatibility, optional release branching and supporting execution docs without changing branding. The PR will map each changed or removed claim to source evidence, explain how the updated tree reaches main, and propose exact GitHub description/topic corrections for explicit owner approval before applying them at merge. Reuse existing documentation, disclosure and positioning checks; no engine or policy change is introduced.

spec:
Owner, verbatim: "Add a goal to update the project README - I noticed drift".

README.md is the front page for users and was last reworked when the new engine landed (G1017 era). Release 1 has since changed what users see, and more lands before the release: consolidated multi-lens reviews (G1022), declared engine capabilities replacing engine.min (G1027), owner questions that block a design for an interview (G1026), git-flow release lines (G1025), merge-based syncing with a squash to tests + implementation commits and conventional commits everywhere (G1038), clean syncs keeping reviews and a round-based budget (G1039), findings carried on re-run cards (G1040), and the project intent (purpose, who it serves, what it is not, principles) the owner approved.

Drift the owner saw, verbatim: "It said it uses GitHub for goal storage". Root's check (2026-11-02):
- dev's README.md and plugin manifests already say goals live on Git branches (zzzops/goal/*).
- The published default branch `main` still carries the pre-reset README ("Goals live in GitHub Issues ...", "stores canonical goals in GitHub Issues"), because Release 1 has not been merged to main yet; it is replaced when the release lands. Confirm the release flow (G1025 release finish) carries dev's README to main and that nothing on main keeps the old text.
- The GitHub repository metadata is wrong and outside Git: description "... manage durable goals in GitHub Issues ..." and topics include `github-issues` and `project-management` (the approved intent says ZzzOps is not a project-management suite). The PR proposes the new description and topics; applying them (`gh repo edit --description ...` plus `--add-topic` / `--remove-topic`) is an external change the owner approves at approve_merge, done at merge.

Scope:
- Audit every claim in README.md against the shipped behaviour on the integration branch at implementation time, and fix or remove each one that has drifted (for example: "the goal's design starts at once with a worker" now may stop for an owner interview; what "human decisions" covers; install and version notes now that engine.min is gone; release branching).
- Make the opening paragraph agree with the approved project intent (settings.intent) without copying it wholesale; keep the README practitioner-first and short.
- Keep links valid; if a linked doc (docs/EXECUTION.md, docs/SKILLS.md, docs/INITIALIZATION.md) has drifted in a way the README depends on, fix that line too or list it for a follow-up goal.
- No new marketing claims; nothing about the owner's private dogfood app.

Acceptance:
- Each changed or removed README claim is listed in the PR body with the code, SPEC section or doc that backs the new wording.
- Links resolve (existing doc link checks pass).
- The owner reviews the wording at approve_merge.
title: Bring the project README back in line with the shipped product
